filters.name: Metals
filters.oneLineSummary: Electropositive elements that lose valence electrons to form cations and basic oxides.

characteristics.title: Metallic Bonding
characteristics.detail: Lattice of positive cations submerged in a sea of delocalized valence electrons.

characteristics.title: Conductivity
characteristics.detail: High electrical and thermal conductivity, metallic luster, malleable and ductile.

characteristics.title: Chemical Nature
characteristics.detail: Strong reducing agents; oxides/hydroxides are basic or amphoteric (Al₂O₃, ZnO).

examTraps: Mercury (Hg) is the only liquid metal at standard room conditions.
Alkali metals (Li, Na, K) can be sliced with a knife and float on water.
Tungsten (W) holds the highest melting point of any metal (3422°C).

filters.name: Non-Metals
filters.oneLineSummary: Electronegative elements that gain or share electrons to form anions or covalent bonds.

characteristics.title: Oxide Character
characteristics.detail: Exclusively acidic (SO₂, CO₂, P₄O₁₀) or neutral (CO, NO, N₂O). Never basic.

characteristics.title: Diverse States
characteristics.detail: Gases (H₂, N₂, O₂, F₂, Cl₂, noble gases), Liquid (Br₂), Solids (C, P, S, I₂).

characteristics.title: Conductivity
characteristics.detail: Poor thermal and electrical conductors due to localized valence electron pairs.

examTraps: Bromine (Br₂) is the only liquid non-metal at standard conditions.
Graphite conducts electricity via delocalized pi-electrons between hexagonal carbon sheets.
Iodine crystals display a lustrous metallic sheen despite being a halogen.

filters.name: Metalloids
filters.oneLineSummary: Staircase borderline elements displaying intermediate metallic and non-metallic behaviors.

characteristics.title: Semiconductivity
characteristics.detail: Electrical conductivity increases with temperature (negative temperature coefficient of resistance).

characteristics.title: Doping Substrates
characteristics.detail: Basis for microelectronics and semiconductors (p-type with B; n-type with P/As).

characteristics.title: Chemical Dualism
characteristics.detail: Form amphoteric or weakly acidic oxides (e.g. As₂O₃, Sb₂O₃).

examTraps: Primary set: B, Si, Ge, As, Sb, Te, Po.
Silicon constitutes ~28% of Earth's crust mass, second only to oxygen.
Unlike metals whose resistance rises with heat, metalloid conductivity improves with temperature.

filters.name: Coinage Metals
filters.oneLineSummary: Group 11 noble transition metals historically used for coinage due to extreme corrosion resistance.

characteristics.title: Members
characteristics.detail: Copper (Cu), Silver (Ag), and Gold (Au).

characteristics.title: Conductivity Peak
characteristics.detail: Silver has the highest electrical and thermal conductivity of all elements, followed by Copper.

characteristics.title: Corrosion Resistance
characteristics.detail: Noble metals resistant to air, moisture, and non-oxidizing acids.

examTraps: Anomalous electron configuration: Cu is 3d¹⁰ 4s¹ (not 3d⁹ 4s²) for d¹⁰ exchange stability.
Zn, Cd, Hg are NOT coinage metals.
Gold dissolves in Aqua Regia (3:1 HCl:HNO₃) to yield soluble [AuCl₄]⁻.

filters.name: Volatile Metals
filters.oneLineSummary: Group 12 metals with completely filled d¹⁰ s² subshells, weak metallic bonds, and low boiling points.

characteristics.title: Members
characteristics.detail: Zinc (Zn), Cadmium (Cd), and Mercury (Hg).

characteristics.title: Weak Lattice
characteristics.detail: No unpaired d-electrons participate in metallic bonding, resulting in unusually low melting/boiling points.

characteristics.title: Pseudo-Transition
characteristics.detail: Often called non-typical transition elements because d-subshell remains full (d¹⁰) in both elemental and +2 ionic states.

examTraps: Mercury (Hg) is liquid at room temperature (MP: -38.8°C).
Zn²⁺, Cd²⁺, Hg²⁺ compounds are strictly diamagnetic and colorless (no d-d transitions).
Amalgams: Mercury dissolves almost all metals except Iron, Platinum, and Tungsten.

filters.name: s-Block Elements
filters.oneLineSummary: Highly reactive, electropositive light metals where differentiating electrons enter the outermost s-orbital.

characteristics.title: Low Ionization Enthalpy
characteristics.detail: Largest atomic radii per period; strong reducing agents.

characteristics.title: Flame Test
characteristics.detail: Impart vivid colors: Li (Crimson), Na (Yellow), K (Lilac), Ca (Brick Red), Ba (Apple Green).

characteristics.title: Oxidation States
characteristics.detail: Strictly fixed +1 (Group 1) and +2 (Group 2); never show variable valency.

examTraps: Be and Mg do NOT give flame colors because their valence electrons are bound too tightly.
Diagonal relationships: Li resembles Mg; Be resembles Al in polarizing power.
Alkali metals in liquid ammonia produce deep blue, conductive, paramagnetic solutions.

filters.name: p-Block Elements
filters.oneLineSummary: The most diverse block containing all non-metals, all metalloids, and post-transition metals.

characteristics.title: Multi-Phase Block
characteristics.detail: Houses metals (Al, Sn, Pb), metalloids (Si, Ge, As), and non-metals (C, O, halogens).

characteristics.title: Inert Pair Effect
characteristics.detail: Reluctance of valence s-electrons to bond in heavier elements (Pb²⁺ > Pb⁴⁺, Tl⁺ > Tl³⁺).

characteristics.title: Oxidation Variety
characteristics.detail: Oxidation states vary in steps of two units; max state = Group number - 10.

examTraps: Inert pair effect makes PbCl₂ stable and PbCl₄ an unstable strong oxidizer.
Fluorine never exhibits positive oxidation states (highest electronegativity, no d-orbitals in 2nd shell).
Carbon has exceptional catenation capability due to strong C-C bond energy (348 kJ/mol).

filters.name: d-Block Elements
filters.oneLineSummary: Transition elements with progressive filling of penultimate (n-1)d orbitals between s and p blocks.

characteristics.title: Variable Valency
characteristics.detail: Both (n-1)d and ns electrons participate in bonding (e.g. Mn shows +2 through +7).

characteristics.title: Colored Compounds
characteristics.detail: d-d orbital splitting in crystal fields absorbs visible wavelengths (Cu²⁺ blue, Fe³⁺ amber).

characteristics.title: Catalytic & Magnetic
characteristics.detail: Unpaired d-electrons impart paramagnetism and high catalytic surface reactivity.

examTraps: Sc³⁺ and Ti⁴⁺ compounds are colorless because their d-subshell is empty (d⁰).
Zn²⁺ is colorless and diamagnetic because its d-subshell is completely full (d¹⁰).
Osmium and Ruthenium exhibit the highest known oxidation state (+8 in OsO₄ and RuO₄).

filters.name: f-Block Elements
filters.oneLineSummary: Inner transition series filling anti-penultimate (n-2)f subshells: 4f (Lanthanides) and 5f (Actinides).

characteristics.title: Common Valency
characteristics.detail: +3 is the universal stable oxidation state for lanthanides.

characteristics.title: Lanthanide Contraction
characteristics.detail: Poor shielding of 4f electrons causes radii to steadily shrink across the row.

characteristics.title: Actinide Radioactivity
characteristics.detail: All actinides are radioactive; transuranics (Z > 92) are synthetic.

examTraps: Due to lanthanide contraction, Zr (4d) and Hf (5d) have identical radii (~160 pm), making separation hard.
Ce⁴⁺ is a powerful analytical oxidizer returning to Ce³⁺.
Promethium (Pm) is the only synthetic/radioactive lanthanide.
